expectations.text: Explains CMMC Level 2 correctly: 110 security requirements drawn from NIST SP 800-171 (Rev 2) protecting Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), codified in the 32 CFR Part 170 program rule
expectations.evidence: "You must implement all 110 practices from NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2, spanning 14 security domains"; "You handle CUI (Controlled Unclassified Information)"; "32 CFR Part 170 and DFARS 252.204-7012/7019/7020/7021 are still the law" explicitly cites 32 CFR 170 as the program rule.

expectations.text: States the July 13, 2026 program status: DoD suspended CMMC Phase 2 — including the C3PAO third-party assessment requirements due in new contracts from November 10, 2026 — pending a 60-day CMMC Reform Task Force review (report due ≈ September 13, 2026); in the interim only Level 1 (Self) or Level 2 (Self) may be designated, and 32 CFR 170 / DFARS clauses remain law (suspension is policy, not repeal)
expectations.evidence: "On July 13, 2026, DoD suspended CMMC Phase 2 — the part of the rollout that would have required third-party (C3PAO) assessments in new contracts starting November 10, 2026... 60-day CMMC Reform Task Force review, with a report due around September 13, 2026... Contracting officers can currently only designate Level 1 (Self) or Level 2 (Self)... 32 CFR Part 170 and DFARS 252.204-7012/7019/7020/7021 are still the law." All elements of the assertion are present, including the policy-not-repeal framing.

expectations.text: Explains prerequisite mechanics that CONTINUE unchanged: SPRS score submission (Basic Assessment against 800-171), SSP requirement, annual senior-official affirmation, and DFARS 252.204-7012 obligations (incl. 72-hour DIBNET incident reporting)
expectations.evidence: "DFARS 252.204-7012 — requires you to safeguard CUI and report cyber incidents to the DoD's DIBNET portal within 72 hours of discovery"; "You calculate a Basic Assessment SPRS score... submit it at sprs.csd.disa.mil, with a senior company official affirming its accuracy — annually"; "Build a System Security Plan (SSP)" listed as step 2.

expectations.text: Gives a realistic readiness timeline for a first-timer (commonly 9-18 months of remediation) and advises HOLDING the remediation course because the task-force outcome may restore third-party assessment on short notice
expectations.evidence: "a commonly cited planning window is 9–18 months from initial gap assessment to being ready for a full third-party (C3PAO) assessment"; "don't slow down. Build your program as if a third-party assessment could still happen — the task force could restore that requirement on short notice."

expectations.text: Recommends concrete first steps: scope where CUI lives, consider an enclave, gap-assess against 800-171, build SSP and POA&M — with C3PAO scheduling framed as paused/on-hold rather than an immediate booking
expectations.evidence: Step-by-step list: "1. Scope your CUI environment... 2. Build a System Security Plan (SSP)... 3. Run a gap assessment against all 110 practices and produce a Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M)"; C3PAO explicitly described as "paused for now" rather than something to book. Note: the response does not use the specific word 'enclave' — it recommends FedRAMP-authorized cloud services and CUI boundary-scoping instead, which is directionally similar but not an explicit enclave recommendation.
